topBar.shortcutLabels: Show or hide the navigation labels

overview.label: Overview
overview.description: This project at a glance, and who is in it.

data.label: Data
data.description: Bring data in and find what is already here.

automate.label: Automate
automate.description: Run work on a schedule and deliver the results.

trust.label: Trust
trust.description: Check the data, act on problems and control access.

share.label: Share
share.description: Charts, dashboards and reports for everyone else.

admin.label: Admin
admin.description: People, organisations and the platform itself.

workspace.label: Home
workspace.description: Everything you can see, across projects.

overview.label: Overview
overview.description: What to do next, recent data and recent runs.
overview.keywords: project home start checklist getting started
help: Follow the checklist to get a project working, one step at a time.
See the newest data and the last few runs.
Add data from here at any time.

activity.label: Activity
activity.description: What happened in this project, newest first.
activity.keywords: activity feed history timeline what happened recent changes log
help: Changes, runs, incidents, comments, alerts and contracts in one list, with who and when.
Choose a kind to see only that.
Each line links to what it is about.

people.label: People
people.description: Who can see and change this project.
people.keywords: members access roles invite team share
help: Add people who already have an account, and choose what each can do.
Viewers can look, operators can run things, editors can change them, admins can manage people.
Removing someone takes away their access to this project only.

alerts.label: Alerts
alerts.description: Where failures and reports are sent: email, Slack or a webhook.
help: Send failures and finished reports to an email address, a Slack channel or your own systems.
Everything already appears in the bell at the top; this adds other places.
Use Send a test to check one works before relying on it.

settings.label: Settings
settings.description: Rename, move, archive or delete this project.
settings.keywords: project settings rename archive delete export import bundle move copy
help: Rename the project or describe what it is for.
Move its recipes, checks, charts and workflows to another project with a bundle.
Archive it when it is no longer used, or delete it when you are sure.

sources.label: Sources
sources.description: Upload files, connect databases and receive live data.
sources.keywords: connect database connection import extraction upload file stream webhook cdc
help: Upload a file: Pipewright shows how it will read it before anything is saved.
Connect a database, browse its tables and import the ones you need.
Set imports to bring in only new rows, so each run is quick.

datasets.label: Datasets
datasets.description: Every table of data in this project.
help: Every table of data in this project, one row per name.
Open one to see its rows and columns, clean it in Studio, or send it somewhere.
Filter by where the data came from, or find one by name.

catalog.label: Catalog
catalog.description: Search datasets by name, column or tag, and keep the glossary.
catalog.keywords: catalogue glossary search find tags owner certified
help: Search datasets by name, by column or by what someone wrote about them.
Keep a glossary so a word like “active customer” means one thing.
Owners and certified datasets show here once people mark them.

studio.label: Studio
studio.description: Clean and reshape a dataset step by step, seeing the result as you go.
studio.keywords: transform clean shape recipe grid spreadsheet steps
help: Pick a dataset and add steps: filter rows, fix text, add columns and more.
Click a step to change it. Right-click a column for steps that suit it.
Every change shows in the preview straight away, and undo takes it back.
Your original data is never changed; save the steps as a recipe to reuse them.

recipes.label: Recipes
recipes.description: Saved recipes: the steps that turn one dataset into another.
help: Recipes are saved sets of steps that turn one dataset into another.
Open one to change its steps in the Studio, or run it to make a fresh result.
Put a recipe on a schedule so it runs by itself.

sql.label: SQL
sql.description: Write SQL against a connected database.
help: Write SQL against a connected database and see the results.
It reads by default; writing needs an administrator.
Save queries you use often.

notebooks.label: Notebooks
notebooks.description: SQL, recipe and note cells that run top to bottom.
help: Mix SQL, recipe and text cells that run from top to bottom.
Each cell can use the result of the cells above it.
Save a notebook to run it again later.

table-editor.label: Table editor
table-editor.description: Edit rows in a connected database table, with a preview before saving.
table-editor.keywords: write back edit rows database table
help: Change rows in a connected database table directly.
You see every change, and how many rows it affects, before it is saved.
Only tables with a clear way to identify each row can be edited.

workflows.label: Workflows
workflows.description: Tasks that run in order, by hand or on a schedule.
help: Chain tasks in order: import, clean, check, deliver.
If a check fails, the tasks after it stop, so bad data goes nowhere.
Run a workflow by hand or on a timetable.

schedules.label: Schedules
schedules.description: Run recipes and deliveries at set times.
help: Run a recipe or a delivery by itself at the times you choose.
Pause a schedule without losing it.
Run now tries it straight away without changing its timetable.

runs.label: Runs
runs.description: Everything that has run in this project, newest first.
help: Everything that has run in this project, newest first.
Filter to failed runs to see what needs attention.
Open a run to see exactly what it did.

destinations.label: Destinations
destinations.description: Databases and file stores that receive your data.
help: Databases and file stores your data can be delivered to.
Test a destination before sending data to it.
Deliveries can run by hand, on a schedule or in a workflow.

bi-tools.label: BI tools
bi-tools.description: Send datasets to Power BI or Tableau.
bi-tools.keywords: bi connections power bi tableau publish
help: Connect Power BI or Tableau.
Send a dataset to them from the dataset’s Send to menu.
Test the connection before relying on it.

checks.label: Checks
checks.description: Rules your data must pass, and their results.
checks.keywords: data quality rules tests validation quarantine
help: Checks are rules your data must pass, such as “every order has an email”.
Run them on a dataset to see which rows fail.
Failing rows can be set aside in their own dataset while the rest carries on.

comparisons.label: Comparisons
comparisons.description: Saved statistical comparisons between two datasets.
help: Saved statistical comparisons between two datasets.
Run one again after the data changes to see if it still holds.

incidents.label: Incidents
incidents.description: Problems that need a person, from failed checks to late data.
help: Problems that need a person: failed checks, late data, unusual numbers.
Acknowledge one to show someone is on it; resolve it when fixed.
Incidents close by themselves when the problem clears.

schema-changes.label: Schema changes
schema-changes.description: Columns added, removed or retyped at a source.
help: Columns added, removed or retyped at a source since the last import.
Breaking changes are marked, because they can stop recipes working.
Acknowledge a change once you have dealt with it.

contracts.label: Contracts
contracts.description: Promises about a dataset that new data must keep.
contracts.keywords: contract promise agreement schema sla freshness consumers follow
help: A contract is a promise about a dataset: its columns, its rows and how often it gets new data.
New data that breaks it is stopped before it replaces what people use.
Follow a contract to be told when it breaks, is kept again or changes.

policies.label: Policies
policies.description: Who sees which rows and columns, and how long data is kept.
policies.keywords: governance security masking retention erasure gdpr
help: Hide rows or columns from some people, or mask sensitive values.
Decide how long old runs and history are kept.
Handle requests to correct or erase someone’s personal data.

approvals.label: Approvals
approvals.description: Changes waiting for someone to approve them.
help: In projects that need approval, changes wait here for someone to accept them.
Running things is never blocked; only changing what they are.
Comment on a change before approving or rejecting it.

audit.label: Audit log
audit.description: Who changed what in this project, and when.
help: Who changed what in this project, and when.
Refused attempts are recorded too.
Filter by person or by what happened.

dashboards.label: Dashboards
dashboards.description: Pages of charts you can share by link or by email.
dashboards.keywords: dashboard bi share link embed iframe portal
help: Pages of charts that answer one question together.
Share a dashboard by link, or have it emailed on a schedule.
Embed it in another site, such as a customer portal.
Filters at the top apply to every chart on it.

charts.label: Charts
charts.description: Ask a question of a dataset and save the answer as a chart.
help: Pick a dataset, what to group by and what to add up.
The preview updates as you change it.
Save a chart, then put it on a dashboard.

reports.label: Reports
reports.description: Files sent by email or Slack on a schedule.
reports.keywords: scheduled reports export excel pdf csv email
help: Send a dataset, chart or dashboard as a file on a timetable.
Excel, CSV, PDF or a web page, by email or Slack.
Each report keeps a history of what was sent.

metrics.label: Metrics
metrics.description: Numbers defined once, so every chart agrees.
help: Define an important number once, such as net revenue.
Charts and reports built on a metric always agree.
Changing a definition keeps a history of the old ones.

accounts.label: Accounts
accounts.description: Everyone who can sign in: invite, reset, deactivate.
accounts.keywords: users people invite admin sign in
help: Everyone who can sign in to this platform.
Invite someone, reset a password, or turn an account off.
Project access is set inside each project, under People.

organisations.label: Organisations
organisations.description: Separate groups of people and projects.
help: Keep separate groups of people and projects apart.
A small team usually needs none.

audit.label: Audit (all projects)
audit.description: Every change across every project, with export.
help: Every change in every project, in one place.
Filter it, and export it for an auditor.

connectors.label: Connectors
connectors.description: Every kind of source the platform can connect to.
help: Every kind of source Pipewright can connect to.
Each shows how well it is tested, so you know what to expect.

status.label: System status
status.description: Whether the platform and its background work are healthy.
help: Whether the platform and its background work are running.
Check here first when runs or schedules seem stuck.

home.label: Home
home.description: What needs attention, and where you left off.
help: What needs attention across your projects.
Jump back into a project, or start a new one.

projects.label: Projects
projects.description: All projects you can open, and a new one.
help: Every project you can open.
Start a new project for a new team or subject.

runs.label: All runs
help: Recent runs across every project you can open.
Filter to failures to see what needs attention anywhere.

datasets.label: Find a dataset
help: Find a dataset by name across every project you can open.

help.label: Help
help.description: How to use Pipewright: getting started, each area, the glossary and the API.

notifications.label: Notifications
notifications.description: Messages about your runs, reports and mentions.

settings.label: Your settings
settings.description: Appearance, password, two-factor sign-in and API tokens.
